name: Evening Dust Primer (Mộ Trần Quyết)
concept: The outer gate's method, practised facing west on the steppe at the old seat for the hour the sun takes to set. The glow of a western evening is the plain's dust lit from below, and the primer teaches an Earth root to breathe that lit dust and a Wood root to breathe the grass as it turns gold. Either root carries a disciple through its six layers. The outer gate sits for it at dusk, an hour a day, by custom; the primer itself turns at any hour. The sixth layer, Dust Holds the Glow, leaves a faint red on the palms after sunset. If the disciple's Earth is strong enough to keep it until full dark, the inner gate opens.
lore: Nhan Cô Vụ taught it from his first year (290) to the herders who came to watch the old man sit in the grass at sunset. It was written down only in 600, when the outer gate grew past what one voice could teach. Since the seat moved in 1185 the outer gate has stayed on the steppe for it.

name: Drifting Sunset Cloud True Canon (Lạc Hà Chân Kinh)

effects.name: The Glow Deepens (Hà Thâm)
effects.rule: A passive art (authored wish d3). Your glow clock is the fight's time plus 1.5 s per damaging blow taken this fight (approximating 1 s per 2 % max health lost to blows; healing never lowers it); for every 6 s on it, your Earth arts deal 4 % more. Its engine record is the Effect of the same name in effects/lac_ha.effects.json; the loader does not yet attach a technique's Effects (pending word technique-effects).

concept: The founder's method and the sect's name, from the line the west is proud of: the sunset clouds and the lone wild duck fly together, and the autumn water is one colour with the long sky. The practitioner lifts Earth qi off the ground as a glowing cloud and keeps it alive with Wood, the way grass holds dust in a dry wind. In a fight the cloud (a Field) grows heavier the longer the fight lasts: while it is up, the foe carries Earth stacks that thicken each breath, you mend a little each breath, and the holder's strikes gain strength the longer the fight runs (the sect calls it the light going). It is slow to start and hard to outlast. Like every method it cultivates faster on land that matches it, and it matches Earth and Wood together: on dry Earth with thin Wood it is slow, and slowest where it is longest, in the upper layers. The founder wrote that warning down. For more than eight hundred years his maples grew round the hall, and no one needed it.
lore: Nhan Cô Vụ wrote it on the steppe in 290-330, when the founding hall stood among the maples he planted (A190). The first copy is written on hemp cloth from Tang Ma Thành and was carried up to the Cloud Bridge in 1185 in the head's own sleeve. Trầm Tịch Dương reached its fourteenth layer before the last seat maple died in 1131. No one has reached its eleventh on the old seat since.

name: Fishing Boats Sing at Dusk (Ngư Chu Xướng Vãn Khúc)
concept: A song art, sung in the reed and maple voice of Wood qi. The river boats of Ngư Ca Xuyên were singing their song at dusk before the sect was founded. Nhan Cô Vụ heard it from the steppe in 290, set Wood qi into it, and gave each village back one verse of the art. Each village kept its verse, and only the inner gate knows all nine. In a fight it is a sustain song: you recover linh lực and shake off fear, and the foe loses a little speed. Since 803 the sect sings it one verse short. The ninth verse is sung only over the dead.
lore: The silence of the boats at dusk in 803 (A197, V091, V095, V103, V104) was the villages refusing to sing the sect's song after Chiết Kích Nguyên. In 805 Nhan Cô Vụ dropped the last verse from the inner gate's teaching, so that the sect would sing one verse fewer, like its villages.

name: Evening Ferry Breathing (Vãn Độ Thổ Nạp Pháp)
concept: A quiet Water and Wood breathing method passed among Lạc Hà's river-born servants: the dyers at the madder vats, the ferryman who rows elders to Tịch Chiếu Đảo, and the lamp-makers' daughters serving the Cloud Bridge guest house. It follows the long pull of an oar and the steam off the dye pot, keeping the breath even through river fog without opening the inner gate.
lore: No elder set it down. It came up the river from Vãn Đăng Thôn and Tang Ma Thành with the weavers and boatmen who served the sect without swearing into its lineage.

name: Bellows and Hearth Breathing (Phong Táo Thổ Nạp Pháp)
concept: The servants' method of Lạc Hà's kitchens and the Tử Điện Thành armoury forge, for Fire hands (kitchen and forge servants) who do not enter the steppe primer. It pairs the steady pull of the bellows with the heat held in a banked hearth, strengthening the body against smoke and embers and warming the blood between shifts.
lore: Taught by word of mouth between Hồ Tứ Nương's kitchen at the old seat and the forge hands of Tử Điện Thành; the Counting House never bothered to price it.

name: Anvil-Thunder Forging Canon (Châm Lôi Đoán Kinh)
concept: A forge-hand's Thunder and Metal method kept by the guest armourer Vưu Chước Kim at Tử Điện Thành. Each heavy hammer blow drives Metal and a spark of Thunder into the target as though setting star-iron on an anvil; once the work holds enough charge or the smith's own iron hide is tempered by blows, a quenching bolt cracks the metal open.
lore: Vưu Chước Kim pieced it together after he left Thối Tinh Môn, folding the lightning of his own root into his old hammer strokes. He teaches it to no one in Lạc Hà, though his forge boy listens from the bellows.

name: Autumn Water and the Long Sky (Thu Thủy Trường Thiên Kinh)

effects.name: Geese Line
effects.rule: A passive art (Nhạn Hàng, d17). While you count two or more allies (you, companions, Pieces), you gain block for each ally beyond yourself.

concept: The elders' war art, named for the second half of the founder's line: the autumn water is one colour with the long sky. The holder spreads Earth and Wood qi across a field until ground, grass and sky look one colour, so a foe inside cannot judge distance or tell which shapes are men. The holder sees clearly. Inside the field the holder's arts strike every foe in it at reduced weight, and foes lose accuracy and hidden things are revealed. It needs a rank: with fewer than three allies standing in the field it is weak, which is why the sect fights as a line and lost at Thiết Tỏa Quan.
lore: Nhan Tề Phi wrote it in 590-610 for the War of the Petal Shore, out of her father's line and the geese of Nhạn Thanh Thành. It won the bay in 620. It also lost the field at Chiết Kích Nguyên in 803, where Quý Trường Kích fought it from inside a ring of halberds. Cảnh Trường Thiên teaches it now, and adds the geese stance Nhạn Trận Môn drills with (V096).
